study: Same-trajectory ignored-backup recovery comparison with agent-rollback
question: Can a checkpoint tool whose Git-aware inventory honors .gitignore recover pre-existing ignored user backups after the same cleanup command deletes them, while preserving the requested cleanup output?
success_contract: Both allowed build artifacts must be absent, and every other project-file path and byte must equal the pre-command baseline.
arms: agent-rollback native checkpoint before command, checkpoint after command, then restore the pre-command checkpoint
C-SDVR production project(base, observed, allowed) projection
pairing: Each arm uses an exact copy of the same Git-initialized baseline, runs the same public command once, and must yield an identical command-post byte map before recovery is scored.
limits: One public cleanup task family with three injected file-count scales; not an independent task cohort.
The injected .gitignore rule and user-backup files create a controlled stress case.
A native CLI result is scoped to the pinned agent-rollback commit and its default Git-aware inventory configuration.
